function: Designs the receive combining vector at the multi-antenna parameter server from training symbols, without channel estimation, to aggregate gradients over the air in federated learning (p. 2-3).
system: Uplink multi-user SIMO: PS with NR=30 to 70 antennas (50 in Fig. 3), K=100 single-antenna devices, block fading, no RIS; frequency band not stated (p. 2, 4-5).
method: Combining vector from sample average approximation, closed-form least squares on M training symbols (Eq. 15); FL model: CNN trained federatedly, Adam, 10 local updates (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Simulated block fading, i.i.d. CN(0,1) entries with path-loss exponent 3.8, devices in 100 m circle; FMNIST and KMNIST for the FL task, 4 classes per device (p. 4).
test_conditions: Same simulated setting for training and testing; Figs. 1-2 sweep M and NR; Fig. 3 uses NR=50, M=70 over 200 rounds; 100 Monte-Carlo trials (p. 4-5).
baselines: Error-free aggregation, LMMSE with perfect CSI, and LMMSE based on LS channel estimation [11] with M=70 and 140; no other published OA-FL design compared (p. 5, Fig. 3).
metrics: Aggregation MSE, probability that the MSE gap to LMMSE is below epsilon, and test accuracy versus M, NR, and rounds on FMNIST and KMNIST (p. 4-5).
complexity: About (2/3)NR^3 + NR^2 M complex operations, versus (2/3)NR^3 + 2K^2 NR + (2/3)K^3 + NR M K + 2K^2 M for LMMSE based on CE (p. 3).
q1_support: p. 4: "i.i.d. drawn from CN(0, 1)" with path-loss exponent 3.8 is a custom Rayleigh model with distance path loss; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 5: "on a varying number of receive antennas" (and of training symbols) is swept, each setting a separate run with its own accuracy; the paper never trains in one condition and tests in another.
q3_support: p. 5: "LMMSE with perfect CSI: the LMMSE estimator in (10)" (classical) and "LMMSE based on CE [11]: the CSI is estimated via LS" (earlier published aggregation design), both compared on test accuracy in Fig. 3.
q4_support: p. 3: "We now discuss the complexity." Counts about (2/3)NR^3 + NR^2 M complex operations for the proposed combiner, versus a larger count for LMMSE based on CE.
q5_support: p. 4: "We use the datasets FMNIST and KMNIST", learning-task datasets only; channels are simulated and no code or data link is given.
notes: Area 7: the problem is over-the-air gradient aggregation through the PS combining vector (p. 2-3). The combining vector is a closed-form SAA least-squares solution (Eq. 15), not a neural network; the learned element is the FL CNN, which passes no_learning under the OA-FL rule. q3 rests on [11] as the earlier published aggregation design and LMMSE with perfect CSI as the classical reference; reviewer to confirm. Complexity formulas read from the page image (p. 3).
